summary: 0/1 new failure modes is diagnosable. The patch swaps deleteWithConfirm for FileUtils.delete in SSTable.delete(), which removes the only error signal for failed file deletions.

findings.problem: The loop now calls FileUtils.delete(String) for every component and ignores its boolean return. Before the patch, every component except SUMMARY went through FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which threw FSWriteError on failure. That error went to the disk failure policy and was logged with the cause. FileUtils.delete(String) is File.delete(). It returns false on failure, with no exception, no log and no metric. A DATA, INDEX or other component that fails to delete (permissions, I/O error, a busy file) now fails silently, and SSTable.delete() still returns true. The SSTable is left partially deleted. This is the same leaked-file and partial-delete state the ticket is trying to fix, and an operator would see no sign of it. It also disables the disk failure policy for these paths. The only message left is the 'Deleting sstable' info line, logged before any deletion happens.
findings.fix: Keep deleteWithConfirm for all components in the sorted loop, so FSWriteError and the failure policy still apply. If SUMMARY needs the old lenient treatment, keep it lenient but log a warn with the file path when delete() returns false. Do not discard the return value.

findings.problem: The new ordering is not visible in telemetry. A component with a missing file reports lastModified()==0, so it sorts first. That is harmless, but nothing logs or traces the order or the timestamps used, so a later REMOVE-record timestamp mismatch at LogFile.verifyRecord cannot be matched against the actual deletion order.
findings.fix: Add a debug or trace log of the deletion order with the per-component timestamps, with the descriptor as context. This is optional and must stay off the info level.
